The arithmetic is right and the headline is wrong. Driving owner-flight at 1440 and pressing 'Add a moment' five times reproduces the claim exactly: 9, 2, 1, 1, 1 days away, three untitled rows on Fri 17 Jul, and the left column changing to 'Nothing is planned until 17 July.' So the pile-up is verified. What is not verified is 'never says so'. The add branch calls openEditor on the new row in the same frame, and the resulting screen states the computed date FOUR times at once: the WHEN field reads '17 July 2026' as an editable value (render-b.js line 827, seeded from iso, thereafter written only by setAway); the stepper readout under it reads 'Friday 17 July 2026 - in 1 day' in a role=status node; the new row on the rail carries the count '1' and the date line 'Fri 17 Jul'; and the row's aria-label via grabLabel carries it again. Focus lands in the title field one Tab from the date, the -7/-1/+1/+7 steppers sit under it, and the undo bar is filled and armed ('A moment was added.' + Undo, Ctrl Z, role=status). A screenshot of the state after five adds shows the WHEN field and the readout occupying the middle of the editing column. This is not a fact manufactured behind the owner's back; it is a default proposed in the most conspicuous editable field on the panel, in the same repaint, with undo already loaded. The only true residue is that the remembered sentence itself omits the day - a single string, not the defect described.

The fix would also make the work worse, and the brief names why: on a measure whose entire thesis is that position IS the date, a moment with date:null cannot be placed. The proposal answers that by inventing a 'No day yet' region at the foot of the measure - a new structural zone, a new rule, a new row treatment, an off-rail limbo for things that are supposedly on the timeline. Then it proposes that 'Done' refuse to close until a day is typed. That refusal is unenforceable as built: the root keydown handler closes the editor on Escape (render-b.js line 1064, closeEditor(root, true)), so the owner escapes and is left with precisely the orphaned undated moment the fix exists to prevent - unless Escape is also disabled, which turns the product's one additive gesture into a modal trap. Worst of all it lands on the empty state: an owner who has just typed '3 October 2026', pressed 'Add a moment' as the very first action they ever take in the product, would now be refused and told to type a second date before anything can exist. Today that path gives them one moment at the halfway mark with the editor open on it - a guess, but a legible, movable one. Trading three untitled rows on tomorrow for a second undatable pile in a region that contradicts the measure is not an improvement at 9.5.

A default date the editor opens on and lets you change is the norm at the named bar - a calendar's new event picks a time you did not choose, Linear's new issue arrives with a state you did not set - and both are correct because the object must exist somewhere before it can be moved. The legitimate criticism buried here is that the seeding RULE degenerates (nearest-minus-seven collapses to tomorrow after three presses), but that is a different finding about a bad default, and this fix does not address it - it deletes the concept of a default instead.
